findings.problem: The hint rules out levantarse but not ponerse de pie, which is also common in Latin America and also means 'to get on your feet', so two answers still fit.
findings.fix: hint: the everyday Latin American verb, not levantarse or ponerse de pie

back.es: pararse: to stand up, to get to your feet (Latin America); also to stop or come to a halt
back.example: Stand up, the teacher has arrived.

note: In Spain the everyday word for standing up is levantarse more than ponerse de pie, so the editor could use "levantarse" in the spain field instead, though either is correct.
